question: A cyclist travels 150 km in 5 hours and then another 90 km in 3 hours. What is the average speed of the cyclist for the entire journey?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Average speed is calculated as the net total distance divided by the total time taken.

Total Distance = 150 + 90 = 240 km

Total Time = 5 + 3 = 8 hours

Average Speed = 240 ÷ 8 = 30 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance covered in first part (D₁) = 150 km

Time taken for first part (T₁) = 5 hours

Distance covered in second part (D₂) = 90 km

Time taken for second part (T₂) = 3 hours

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = (Total Distance) ÷ (Total Time)

 Average Speed Journey
 
•

 Total Distance = 240 km | Total Time = 8 hrs

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = D₁ + D₂

⇒ Total Distance = 150 + 90 = 240 km

⇒ Total Time = T₁ + T₂

⇒ Total Time = 5 + 3 = 8 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 240 ÷ 8

⇒ Average Speed = 30 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 30 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

If two equal distances are covered at speeds x and y respectively, then the Average Speed over the entire journey = (2xy) ÷ (x + y).

Conversion of Units

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply the value by 18/5.

Relative Speed

When two bodies are moving in opposite directions, relative speed = (x + y). When moving in the same direction, relative speed = |x − y|.
